entries.prompt: Framing-only correction of this exact isolated Temple Guard mask. Keep identical camera, proportions, ornament rim, two forehead relief dots, pale solid eye lenses, sculpt, paint and all visible details. Do not redesign or change material. The mask is now too close to top and bottom. Make the entire mask only about8% smaller, uniformly preserving aspect ratio, and center it vertically in the same square1254x1254 transparent canvas. Aim at approximately10% EMPTY transparent padding above the topmost ornamental rim and below the bottommost cheek/muzzle, retaining every edge. No crop, no new biological frill, no new spikes, no extra ribs, no dreads/skin/neck/body/collar or backdrop. One complete mask, no shadows/text. Genuine transparent RGBA, same subtle source-view camera, no frontalization or rotation. Do not add grain or new wear.
entries.sourceGenerationPrompt:
Create ONE isolated rigid mask A from the actual photographed licensed toy edition: NECA Temple Guard Series15 final catalogue shown April2016, licensed Alien vs. Predator2004toy edition. Reference1 controls the visible source camera, tilt, sculpture, asymmetries, proportions, paint palette and wear. Other references if present only corroborate this same edition, not another view to merge. Do not substitute a PHG interpretation, another edition or a generic Predator mask.

Use ONLY the brown/grey metallic MASK WORN by the main catalogue figure explicitly identified by the publisher as TEMPLE GUARD, not Ancient Warrior or Scar. Keep its actual near-front downward-pitched source view and compact proportions. Retain the broad short domed metal forehead with its REAL ORNAMENTAL RADIAL SCALLOPED/RIBBED UPPER RIM, two small genuine round relief marks on the forehead, the angular layered heavy brow, two cool pale grey solid eye lenses, broad plain rounded cheek housings and one short rounded central dark-silver front/snouthousing. The scalloped bronze/brown rim is documented hard mask ornamentation and must be kept as it appears, not extended into new antlers or smoothed away. Distinguish the actual ribbed metal rim from any living head material behind it; remove only living skin/cranium and dreadlocks/neck. Keep real muted dark bronze/brown/grey patinated paint and silver edge scuffs; no bright gold/chrome, new runes, extra ribs/horns/vents, or teeth. Remove body armor/necklace, hands, cannon and weapons.

Remove every wearer component: living skin/cranium, eyes or teeth behind the mask, biological mandibles, all dreadlocks and their bands, neck, collar, body/chest/shoulder armor, shoulder cannon, cables/hoses belonging to the wearer, hands, weapons, mannequin/stand, scene/catalogue background and any unrelated separate heads or accessories. Keep only the complete rigid mask sculpture. Preserve solid lens materials and real recessed vents; do not expose or invent a living mouth. No new hidden rear/interior geometry or new profile. No forced frontalization, symmetrization, stretching or rotation from the selected source camera. No invented runes, letters, extra horns, tusks, holes, vents, or paint.

For A follow the actual source paint and neutral catalogue lighting where provided; do not create a new colourway. Preserve real sculpted relief and weathered finish, but do not add fictional microdetail to fake source resolution. One whole mask only, genuine transparent alpha, no floor, support, cast-shadow plane, labels/text/grid or duplicate. Request1254x1254square if supported; mask78–80percent of largest canvas axis with8–12percent clear margins all sides and no clipped edge. This is a documented photographed edition study, not canonical film-prop or human-art certification.
